label: prf:substrate-parameter-unique
title: Proof of uniqueness of the substrate parameter
html:
Suppose q, q' \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) are both substrate parameters for the same QOU (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau). Each extracts from the same braiding c_{V,V} via the spectral decomposition of existence.

Step 1 (spectral data is intrinsic). The rigid monoidal structure and the volume constraint \epsilon \colon \Lambda^2 V \twoheadrightarrow \mathbf{1} determine the canonical splitting V \otimes V = S^2 V \oplus \Lambda^2 V uniquely as the eigenspace decomposition of c_{V,V} under the induced H_2(q)-action (the braiding generates the two-strand Iwahori--Hecke algebra, the q-deformation of S_2); neither summand involves a choice. Hence the eigenvalues \lambda_+, \lambda_- \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) of c_{V,V} on S^2 V and \Lambda^2 V are intrinsic invariants.

Step 2 (Hecke relation pins eigenvalue pair). By braiding eigenvalue extraction, c_{V,V} satisfies (T - \lambda_+)(T - \lambda_-) = 0 with \lambda_+ \lambda_- = -1. Thus the unordered pair \{\lambda_+, \lambda_-\} = \{q, -q^{-1}\} is determined by the QOU, so q \in \{\lambda_+, -\lambda_-^{-1}\}, and the same for q'.

Step 3 (positivity pins the sign). The positive-definite dagger structure induced by (\int_A, S) forces q \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}: the q-eigenvalue of the symmetric braiding channel must be strictly positive because \langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_q = \int_A \circ \mu \circ (S \otimes c_{V,V}) is positive definite only when the S^2 V-eigenvalue is positive. The same constraint applies to q'.

Step 4 (conclusion). From Step 2, q, q' \in \{\lambda_+, -\lambda_-^{-1}\}; from Step 3 both are positive. Since \lambda_+ > 0 and -\lambda_-^{-1} = q (from \lambda_+ \lambda_- = -1), the two candidates coincide: q = q' = \lambda_+. In the archimedean realisation, the same argument applies pointwise on M, so the substrate field q \colon M \to \mathbb{R}_{>0} is uniquely determined by the QOU data. \square
